execution_overview.overall_summary: Both tasks support the focal claim under the revised conclusion rule. Task1 is weak/directional support because the coefficient is positive but not statistically significant; Task2 is strong support because the coefficient is positive and statistically significant.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: The agent followed the planned Task1 path exactly: OLS of log wage gain on all education groups with college degree as the reference, country fixed effects, and HC3 robust standard errors. No implementation repairs or analytic deviations were made.

result_raw.metric: OLS coefficient: log wage gain difference, never_high_school versus college_degree
result_raw.result_text: With country fixed effects, immigrants in the never-high-school group had an estimated 0.188 log-point larger wage gain than immigrants with a college degree, corresponding to about a 20.6% larger gain, but the 95% confidence interval included zero and the two-sided p-value was 0.254.

conclusion.rule_applied: Support if the focal estimate is in the expected direction; strong support if it is also statistically significant. Opposite requires affirmative material contrary evidence, not sign alone.
conclusion.uncertainty_statement: The estimate is in the claimed positive direction, but the 95% confidence interval includes zero and the two-sided p-value is 0.254.
conclusion.conclusion_text: Task1 supports the focal claim: the focal coefficient is positive. Its p-value is above 0.05, so the support is weak/directional rather than strong.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: The agent followed the planned Task2 path exactly: pooled OLS of log wage gain on all education groups with college degree as the reference, no sector controls, no region controls, no country fixed effects, and HC3 robust standard errors. No implementation repairs or analytic deviations were made.

result_raw.metric: OLS coefficient: log wage gain difference, never_high_school versus college_degree
result_raw.result_text: In the pooled no-sector/no-region model, immigrants in the never-high-school group had an estimated 0.260 log-point larger wage gain than immigrants with a college degree, corresponding to about a 29.7% larger gain. The 95% confidence interval was entirely positive and the two-sided p-value was 0.031.

conclusion.rule_applied: Support if the focal estimate is in the expected direction; strong support if it is also statistically significant. Opposite requires affirmative material contrary evidence, not sign alone.
conclusion.uncertainty_statement: The estimate is in the claimed positive direction, the 95% confidence interval excludes zero, and the two-sided p-value is 0.031.
conclusion.conclusion_text: Task2 supports the focal claim because the focal coefficient is positive and statistically significant.
